guideTitle: The Best HDMI Portable Monitors for Consoles, Older Laptops and PCs
metaTitle: Best HDMI Portable Monitors for Consoles and Older Laptops (2026)
metaDescription: We compared 15.6-inch HDMI portable monitors on full-size versus mini-HDMI, power setup, stand design, VESA mounting and warranty, for consoles, desktops and laptops without USB-C video.
introParagraphs: An HDMI portable monitor is the answer when your device cannot send video over USB-C: consoles such as the PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, many desktop graphics cards and older laptops. Every monitor here accepts HDMI, but the port differs. Some use full-size HDMI, which takes a standard cable; others use mini-HDMI, which needs the right cable or an adapter.

The other practical point is power. HDMI carries no power, so when you connect over HDMI each of these monitors also needs a USB cable to a wall adapter or powered port. Stands differ too: folding covers, built-in kickstands, or VESA holes for a monitor arm.
All seven are 15.6-inch 1080p IPS monitors. Our comparison is based on published specifications, included accessories, warranty terms and price position, not hands-on testing.

kyy-156-1080p-portable-monitor-cover.summary: A widely reviewed 15.6-inch 1080p monitor with mini-HDMI, two USB-C ports and a cover-stand.
kyy-156-1080p-portable-monitor-cover.description:
The KYY with smart cover is the sensible all-rounder: a 15.6-inch 1080p IPS panel with two USB-C ports and mini-HDMI, and a mini-HDMI-to-HDMI cable in the box. It is the most widely reviewed monitor here.

At 1.7 lb and 0.3 inches thick it travels easily, and it has built-in speakers and a headphone jack. The magnetic cover doubles as a stand with two angle positions.

The mini-HDMI port ties you to the included cable or an adapter, and on HDMI it still needs USB power.
kyy-156-1080p-portable-monitor-cover.bestFor: Most buyers connecting a laptop, phone or console, at home or on the move.
kyy-156-1080p-portable-monitor-cover.skipIf: You want a standard HDMI port; the UPERFECT or cocopar have full-size HDMI.

cocopar-156-1080p-vesa-mountable.summary: Full-size HDMI, two USB-C ports, 85% sRGB and VESA mounting holes.
cocopar-156-1080p-vesa-mountable.description:
The cocopar is the step up: a full-size HDMI port with two full-featured USB-C ports, a panel listed at 85 percent sRGB, and VESA mounting holes on the back for a monitor arm. It is also the best-rated monitor here.

It weighs 1.5 lb without its case and includes a smart stand case.

It is the most expensive monitor here at the time of writing, the case adds weight (2.4 lb together), and it still needs USB power over HDMI.
cocopar-156-1080p-vesa-mountable.bestFor: Buyers who want full-size HDMI, better color on paper and arm mounting.
cocopar-156-1080p-vesa-mountable.skipIf: Price matters most; the UPERFECT has full-size HDMI and VESA for much less.

uperfect-156-fhd-vesa-otg.summary: Full-size HDMI, dual USB-C, an OTG port and a 75 x 75mm VESA mount for about $66.
uperfect-156-fhd-vesa-otg.description:
The UPERFECT is the value pick for consoles, desktop graphics cards and older PCs: a standard full-size HDMI input, two USB-C ports, an OTG port for a mouse or keyboard, and a 75 x 75mm VESA mount.

It has a flicker-free backlight, built-in speakers and a lined smart cover, and it is well reviewed for its price.

The listing does not clearly confirm USB-C video (DisplayPort Alt Mode), so treat HDMI as the main video input, and it needs USB power over HDMI.
specs: Inputs: full-size HDMI, 2 x USB-C, OTG
uperfect-156-fhd-vesa-otg.bestFor: Consoles, desktops and older laptops that output full-size HDMI.
uperfect-156-fhd-vesa-otg.skipIf: You mainly connect a USB-C laptop; the KYY supports USB-C clearly.

asus-zenscreen-mb169ck-156.summary: ASUS's ZenScreen with a three-year warranty, TÜV eye-care certification and a 360° kickstand.
asus-zenscreen-mb169ck-156.description:
The ASUS ZenScreen MB169CK is the choice if warranty and build matter: ASUS backs it for three years, the longest here, and lists TÜV certification for low blue light and flicker-free operation.

A 360-degree kickstand replaces the folding cover, it has a tripod socket, and ASUS's auto-rotate software helps with portrait use on Windows. Inputs are two USB-C ports and mini-HDMI.

Mini-HDMI means checking your cable, and it costs more than the KYY and UPERFECT without a large specification advantage.
specs: TÜV low blue light and flicker-free
asus-zenscreen-mb169ck-156.bestFor: Buyers who value a longer warranty and an established brand.
asus-zenscreen-mb169ck-156.skipIf: You want full-size HDMI; the UPERFECT costs less and has it.

arzopa-156-fhd-kickstand.summary: A metal-bodied monitor with a kickstand built into the housing and listed console support.
arzopa-156-fhd-kickstand.description:
The ARZOPA builds its kickstand into the metal housing, so there is no cover to carry or lose. It supports duplicate, extend and second-screen modes, and ARZOPA lists compatibility with PS4, PS5, Xbox and Switch as well as computers.

It weighs 1.6 lb and is well rated by buyers.

The listing does not specify full-size or mini-HDMI, so check before buying for a console, and it has no VESA mount.
specs: Inputs: USB-C and HDMI (port size not specified)
arzopa-156-fhd-kickstand.bestFor: People who set the monitor up often and want the stand built in.
arzopa-156-fhd-kickstand.skipIf: You want to mount it on an arm; the cocopar or UPERFECT have VESA holes.

kyy-156-fhd-gaming-hdmi-cable-included.summary: A KYY with HDR mode, HDMI and USB-C cables and a screen protector in the box.
kyy-156-fhd-gaming-hdmi-cable-included.description:
This KYY is the pick if you want everything for a console in the box: it includes a mini-HDMI-to-HDMI cable, two USB-C cables and a screen protector, and adds an HDR mode with a listed 1000:1 contrast ratio.

It otherwise matches the top KYY: 1.7 lb, 0.3 inches thick, two USB-C ports, mini-HDMI and a two-angle folding cover, for the same price at the time of writing.

The port is still mini-HDMI, and it needs USB power over HDMI.
specs: Includes mini-HDMI cable, 2 USB-C cables, screen protector
pros: Same price as the top KYY
kyy-156-fhd-gaming-hdmi-cable-included.bestFor: Console players who want all the cables included.
kyy-156-fhd-gaming-hdmi-cable-included.skipIf: You want full-size HDMI; the UPERFECT has it.

mnn-156-fhd-budget-usb-c-hdmi.summary: A 15.6-inch 1080p monitor with HDR mode, two USB-C ports and HDMI for about $50.
mnn-156-fhd-budget-usb-c-hdmi.description:
The MNN is the lowest-priced monitor here at about $50 at the time of writing, with a 1080p IPS panel, an HDR mode, two full-featured USB-C ports and HDMI, and a smart cover that doubles as a stand.

It supports copy, extended and portrait modes and has a large review base for its price.

Buyer feedback is a little weaker than for the other picks, the listing does not confirm full-size or mini-HDMI, and there is no VESA mount.
specs: Inputs: 2 x USB-C, HDMI (size not specified)
mnn-156-fhd-budget-usb-c-hdmi.skipIf: You need to know the HDMI port type for a console; choose a model that states it.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Full-size HDMI (cocopar, UPERFECT) takes a standard cable from a console or graphics card. Mini-HDMI (both KYYs, ASUS) needs the right cable. The ARZOPA and MNN listings do not specify.
HDMI carries no power. Plan for a USB cable to a wall adapter or powered port whenever you use HDMI.
Folding covers are light but offer few angles; kickstands (ASUS, ARZOPA) are always attached; VESA holes (cocopar, UPERFECT) allow a monitor arm.
The KYY monitors include a mini-HDMI-to-HDMI cable; the KYY console bundle adds USB-C cables and a screen protector.
The ASUS lists three years, the longest here. Check the other listings for warranty terms.

faq.q: Does an HDMI portable monitor need its own power?
faq.a: Yes. HDMI carries video only, so each monitor here needs a USB cable to a wall adapter, powered USB port or second port on your device when using HDMI.

faq.q: Can I use a USB-C-only portable monitor with a PS5 or Xbox?
faq.a: Not directly. Those consoles output video over HDMI, so you need a monitor with an HDMI input like the ones here.

faq.q: What's the difference between full-size and mini-HDMI?
faq.a: Full-size HDMI takes a standard cable. Mini-HDMI is smaller and needs a mini-HDMI-to-HDMI cable or adapter. The cocopar and UPERFECT use full-size; both KYYs and the ASUS use mini-HDMI.

faq.q: Which monitor is easiest to set up for a console?
faq.a: The KYY console bundle includes the cables you need. If you prefer a standard HDMI port, the UPERFECT avoids adapters.

faq.q: Can I mount a portable monitor on an arm?
faq.a: Only if it has VESA holes. Here, the cocopar and UPERFECT (75 x 75mm) do; the others rely on a cover or kickstand.

faq.q: What refresh rate will I get?
faq.a: All seven are 1080p 60Hz monitors, which suits office work and most console play.

bottomLine: For most people, the KYY with smart cover is the proven all-rounder, and its console bundle version adds all the cables. If you want a standard HDMI port, the UPERFECT is the value choice with VESA mounting, and the cocopar adds better listed color at a higher price.

The ASUS ZenScreen is worth paying more for if you want a three-year warranty and a sturdy kickstand, the ARZOPA suits anyone who wants the stand built in, and the MNN is the budget option, though check its HDMI port type before relying on it for a console.
